finding_statement: The 41 CMAs contain 1,009,239 SME employer locations; the median CMA has 7,986 and the largest (Toronto) has 264,670.
limitation: locations, not businesses or clients
implication_for_phase_i: scale needs a log or rank-free robust transform before any comparison

finding_statement: SME locations are concentrated: the 3 largest CMAs hold 52.1% and the 5 largest 64.1% of the 41-CMA total; 3 CMAs account for half.
limitation: CMA boundaries differ in extent; 41 CMAs are not all of Canada
implication_for_phase_i: a raw-count scale indicator would be dominated by 3 markets

finding_statement: The 1-499 band is 99.54% to 99.91% of employer locations in every CMA.
evidence_measure: C02 SME share of employer locations
limitation: 500+ locations are few; share is near-constant
implication_for_phase_i: C02 does not discriminate between markets (rejected)

finding_statement: Unclassified locations are 6.7% of SME locations at the median CMA (range 4.3% to 12.7%; highest: St. John's).
limitation: Unclassified is never allocated to sectors
implication_for_phase_i: use as an industry-evidence guardrail

finding_statement: Public administration (NAICS 91) is 0.35% of SME locations at the median CMA, up to 2.10% (Fredericton); it is excluded from the 19-sector denominator.
limitation: outside SME banking scope
implication_for_phase_i: context only

finding_statement: Median SME locations: Tier 1 15,429, Tier 2 5,603, Tier 3 4,060; Tier 1 holds 90.4% of the 41-CMA total.
limitation: tiers were defined by evidence coverage, not size
implication_for_phase_i: tier and scale are confounded; test scale within the 35-CMA set

finding_statement: Across 35 CMAs the 12-month mean monthly opening rate ranges 2.59% to 5.90% (median 4.48%); closure rate median 4.38%.
statistical_unit: monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1)
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: all-employer-business momentum context
implication_for_phase_i: rates are comparable across CMAs; label as all-employer context

finding_statement: 27 of 35 CMAs had a positive 12-month mean net-formation rate; the median was 0.033% per month.
statistical_unit: monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1)
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: all-employer-business momentum context
implication_for_phase_i: net formation is small relative to gross flows; small differences may be noise

finding_statement: Net-formation rate rose versus the prior 12 months in 22 of 35 CMAs; 0 of 35 changes exceed the 2-SE noise heuristic.
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05 vs 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; prior 12 months 2024-06 to 2025-05
limitation: month-to-month noise; regression to the mean
implication_for_phase_i: treat acceleration as a candidate with a stability check, not a standalone signal

finding_statement: The 36-month linear trend in net-formation rate is positive in 16 of 35 CMAs.
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 36 months 2023-06 to 2026-05
limitation: linear fit; not a forecast
implication_for_phase_i: compare C08 and C09 for consistency before choosing one

finding_statement: Summed 12-month net formation differs from the change in active enterprises (median absolute gap 12 enterprises).
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: reopenings, exits and separate seasonal adjustment are not in openings - closures
implication_for_phase_i: C06 and C07 are different quantities; do not use one to validate the other

finding_statement: Month-to-month volatility of net-formation rate ranges 0.173% to 0.724% (12-month SD); highest in Abbotsford - Mission.
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: smaller CMAs have noisier rates
implication_for_phase_i: volatility vs scale Spearman rho = -0.64; control for size if used

finding_statement: All 35 eligible CMAs have 12 of 12 usable months for every core momentum series; 0 E-flagged and 0 unavailable observations in the recent window.
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: pandemic months are outside the windows
implication_for_phase_i: momentum coverage is sufficient for the 35-CMA decision set

finding_statement: Complete 12-month opening and closing rates exist for the 1-4 band in 35 CMAs and for the 5-19 band in 22; active counts for 5-19 are complete in 35.
statistical_unit: monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1)
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: bands are not an SME total and say nothing about 20-499
implication_for_phase_i: 1-4 rate is testable on 35 CMAs; 5-19 would bias comparisons (13 missing)

finding_statement: The largest SME sector is 'Health care and social assistance' in 17 of 41 CMAs.
limitation: shares use the classified 19-sector denominator
implication_for_phase_i: sector mix is broadly similar; specialization is the distinguishing signal

finding_statement: Sector HHI ranges 0.085 (Brantford, most diversified) to 0.105 (Ottawa - Gatineau, most concentrated); effective number of sectors 9.6 to 11.8.
limitation: narrow range; direction of preference not established
implication_for_phase_i: Phase I must decide whether diversification is desirable

finding_statement: 47 CMA x sector cells are materially over-represented (LQ >= 1.5, >= 10 locations, |z| >= 3); the largest is Mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction in Red Deer (LQ 8.81, 90 locations).
limitation: benchmark is the 41-CMA universe, not Canada
implication_for_phase_i: specialization informs sector targeting, not market comparison

finding_statement: 39 of 779 CMA x business-sector cells have fewer than 10 SME locations; their shares and LQs are unstable.
limitation: small counts inflate LQ swings
implication_for_phase_i: require minimum counts for any sector-level indicator

finding_statement: 1-4 employee locations are 51.8% of SME locations at the median CMA (range 43.1% to 64.3%); 100-499 is 1.95%.
limitation: location-based, not enterprise size
implication_for_phase_i: size mix varies modestly; direction must be set by product strategy

finding_statement: 3 CMAs have a size-band share at least 2 SD from the 41-CMA mean: Saguenay (20-99), Trois-Rivières (20-99), Toronto (1-4;5-19).
limitation: z-scores on 41 observations; descriptive only
implication_for_phase_i: flag distinct profiles; do not treat as preference

finding_statement: The smallest CMA-level 100-499 count is 55 locations (Nanaimo); at CMA x sector x 100-499 only 37.4% of cells have 10+ locations (Phase F).
limitation: the analytical views do not hold the CMA x sector x size cross
implication_for_phase_i: 100-499 is usable at CMA level only

finding_statement: The national external-financing request rate is 49.3%; 4 of 24 usable CMA estimates are distinguishable from it, and 40 of 276 CMA pairs.
limitation: sampling error; segment-vs-national test is conservative
implication_for_phase_i: CMA survey differences are mostly not distinguishable: keep ISED as context

finding_statement: The national debt request rate is 25.7%; 2 of 24 usable CMA estimates are distinguishable from it, and 26 of 276 CMA pairs.
limitation: sampling error; segment-vs-national test is conservative
implication_for_phase_i: CMA survey differences are mostly not distinguishable: keep ISED as context

finding_statement: Product-level approval rates at CMA level include 20 F and 19 E estimates out of 96.
limitation: small requester samples
implication_for_phase_i: reject CMA-level product approval rates as indicators

finding_statement: Six Tier 3 CMAs have scale and composition evidence but no 0722 momentum history; they stay visible and are excluded from momentum comparisons.
limitation: scale-only; not eligible for the primary momentum-based comparison
implication_for_phase_i: Phase I must define how Tier 3 appears (for example, a separate scale-only view)

finding_statement: scale vs net-formation rate: Spearman rho = 0.08 (n = 35).
statistical_unit: location (employer statistical location) vs monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1)
period: 1097 December 2025 (REF_DATE 2025-07) | 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: association, not causation
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: opening rate vs net-formation rate: Spearman rho = -0.01 (n = 35).
statistical_unit: monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1) vs monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1)
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05 | 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: arithmetic identity: net-formation rate = opening rate - closure rate
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: closure rate vs net-formation rate: Spearman rho = -0.13 (n = 35).
statistical_unit: monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1) vs monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1)
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05 | 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05
limitation: arithmetic identity: net-formation rate = opening rate - closure rate
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: recent net-formation level vs change: Spearman rho = 0.59 (n = 35).
statistical_unit: monthly rate (enterprises per active enterprise at t-1) vs rate difference (monthly rate units)
period: 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05 | 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; trailing 12 months 2025-06 to 2026-05 vs 0722 monthly, seasonally adjusted; prior 12 months 2024-06 to 2025-05
limitation: recent level vs change: regression-to-the-mean risk
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: scale vs sector concentration: Spearman rho = -0.16 (n = 41).
statistical_unit: location (employer statistical location) vs index (0-1) of location shares
limitation: association, not causation
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: scale vs micro-location share: Spearman rho = 0.61 (n = 41).
statistical_unit: location (employer statistical location) vs share of locations
limitation: association, not causation
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: external-financing vs debt request rate: Spearman rho = 0.44 (n = 24).
statistical_unit: survey estimate (% of SMEs) vs survey estimate (% of SMEs)
period: ISED SFGSME 2023 survey (calendar 2023) | ISED SFGSME 2023 survey (calendar 2023)
affected_market_or_segment: 24 Tier 1 CMAs (ISED CMA estimates, usable only)
limitation: both shares of all SMEs in the segment (same survey universe)
implication_for_phase_i: not redundant at the 0.8 threshold

finding_statement: 13 of 24 quantitative candidates have Tukey extremes; none are removed or winsorized.
limitation: Tukey fences on 24-41 observations are indicative only
implication_for_phase_i: Phase I to choose robust scaling; do not delete markets
